chunks: Indeed, the two arbitrators were appointed to revive what the Qur'an revives and to destroy what the Qur'an destroys.
Its revival is unity upon it, and its destruction is division from it.
If the Qur'an drives us to them, we follow them; and if it drives them to us, they follow us.
I did not bring you misfortune, nor did I deceive you in your matter, nor did I confuse it for you.
Your own group unanimously suggested the choice of two men.
We bound them that they would not exceed the Qur'an.
But they deviated from it, and abandoned the truth while both of them were aware of it.
And injustice was their desire, so they proceeded upon it.
And our exclusion of them had preceded—in judging with justice and adhering to the truth—their evil opinion and the injustice of their verdict.
ai.seo_question: Why did the two arbitrators fail to uphold the Qur'an according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that the arbitrators were appointed to revive the Qur'an's authority, yet they deviated due to personal desire (hawa) and injustice, effectively nullifying their mandate. This passage is pivotal in Shia historiography for critiquing the validity of the Siffin arbitration, emphasizing that their failure to adhere strictly to the Qur'an revealed their inherent bias and political maneuvering rather than genuine judicial impartiality.
